questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the limits, solving $y_{2}=y_{1}$ if they are not given**
$6-x^{2}=2$
$x^{2}=4$
$x=-2,\ 2$
2. **Decide which curve gives the outer radius and which gives the inner radius**
At $x=0$: $6>2$, so $y=6-x^{2}$ is the outer radius.
3. **Evaluate $\pi\int\left(\text{outer}^{2}-\text{inner}^{2}\right)$ over each interval**
$V=\pi\int_{-2}^{2}\left[\left(6-x^{2}\right)^{2}-4\right]dx$
$= \pi\int_{-2}^{2}\left(32-12x^{2}+x^{4}\right)dx$
$= 2\pi\left[32x-4x^{3}+\dfrac{x^{5}}{5}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$= 2\pi\left(64-32+\dfrac{32}{5}\right)$
$= \dfrac{384\pi}{5}\ \text{units}^{3}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the limits, solving $y_{2}=y_{1}$ if they are not given**
$3x=x^{2}$
$x=0,\ 3$, so the region runs from $y=0$ to $y=9$.
2. **Decide which curve gives the outer radius and which gives the inner radius**
$y=x^{2}$ gives $x=\sqrt{y}$ and $y=3x$ gives $x=\dfrac{y}{3}$.
At $y=1$: $1>\dfrac{1}{3}$, so $x=\sqrt{y}$ is the outer radius.
3. **Evaluate $\pi\int\left(\text{outer}^{2}-\text{inner}^{2}\right)$ over each interval**
$V=\pi\int_{0}^{9}\left(y-\dfrac{y^{2}}{9}\right)dy$
$= \pi\left[\dfrac{y^{2}}{2}-\dfrac{y^{3}}{27}\right]_{0}^{9}$
$= \pi\left(\dfrac{81}{2}-27\right)$
$= \dfrac{27\pi}{2}\ \text{units}^{3}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the limits, solving $y_{2}=y_{1}$ if they are not given**
$x=x^{3}$
$x\left(1-x^{2}\right)=0$
For $x\ge 0$: $x=0,\ 1$
2. **Decide which curve gives the outer radius and which gives the inner radius**
At $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$: $\dfrac{1}{2}>\dfrac{1}{8}$, so $y=x$ is the outer radius.
3. **Evaluate $\pi\int\left(\text{outer}^{2}-\text{inner}^{2}\right)$ over each interval**
$V=\pi\int_{0}^{1}\left(x^{2}-x^{6}\right)dx$
$= \pi\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3}-\dfrac{x^{7}}{7}\right]_{0}^{1}$
$= \pi\left(\dfrac{1}{3}-\dfrac{1}{7}\right)$
$= \dfrac{4\pi}{21}\ \text{units}^{3}$

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the limits, solving $y_{2}=y_{1}$ if they are not given**
The inner curve only exists for $x\ge 1$, so the region splits at $x=1$.
2. **Decide which curve gives the outer radius and which gives the inner radius**
$y=\sqrt{x}$ is the outer radius throughout; the inner radius is $0$ before $x=1$ and $\sqrt{x-1}$ after it.
3. **Evaluate $\pi\int\left(\text{outer}^{2}-\text{inner}^{2}\right)$ over each interval**
$\pi\int_{0}^{1}x\,dx = \pi\left[\dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$\pi\int_{1}^{3}\left[x-(x-1)\right]dx = \pi\int_{1}^{3}1\,dx = 2\pi$
$V=\dfrac{\pi}{2}+2\pi$
$= \dfrac{5\pi}{2}\ \text{units}^{3}$
